subject: Re: Next steps — stakeholder map & champion enablement for FinServe POC
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinServe discovery — initial stakeholder map and asks

Thanks for joining the call earlier. Quick recap from my notes and immediate asks so we can enable our champion internally and externally:

Attendees (FinServe): Dana Lewis (Head of AI Programs), Mike Turner (Infrastructure / Procurement), Jasmin Patel (Legal).
Attendees (Redwood): me (AE), Neha (Solutions), Marissa (CS lead) joined briefly.

Key takeaways:
- Business problem: FinServe wants to reduce per-transaction ML latency for fraud scoring and cut inference costs by ~30% vs their current hosted provider.
- Scale: ~1.2M inference requests/month, 1.5s SLAs for synchronous scoring in peak windows.
- Decision criteria: latency SLOs, predictable unit economics, SOC2 & data residency, contract length (12–24 mo).
- Procurement timeline: procurement review by 2026-03-20, budget approval by 2026-03-25 (Dana).
- Security asks: SOC2 report, data retention policy, KMS/HSM support, audit logs

Immediate next steps (from call):
1) Build a short champion playbook for Dana that includes one-slide ROI, 3 talk tracks for Procurement/Security/Infra, and a list of asks from Procurement/Legal.
2) Share SOC2 + SLC appendix with Jasmin; Mike wants a one-page procurement checklist.
3) Draft a lightweight MoA/SOW template they can use for the POC (2–4 week POC; we proposed sample scope).

Can you take the playbook + ROI estimate (Marissa: pricing and run-rate impact) and I’ll intro to Dana and loop Procurement/Legal? Timeboxed — can we have drafts by Monday 2026-03-09 EOD PT?

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Attachments referenced: none in this note.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinServe discovery — initial stakeholder map and asks

Thanks Rishi — good notes. I’ll own the champion playbook + procurement checklist. Marissa, can you pull together the ROI spreadsheet (one-tab) with the following lines: current monthly inference spend (vendor), projected Redwood spend (with batching/caching + quantization across 3 model variants), estimated token savings, and expected latency P95 change? Keep assumptions explicit.

Champion playbook outline (short):
- One-line value prop for Dana: "Deliver predictable, low-latency fraud scoring at ~30% lower unit cost with enterprise controls and SOC2 support."
- Three audience-specific talk tracks:
  * Economic buyer (Dana / CFO): total cost of ownership, predictable unit economics, committed reserved pricing vs on-demand, measured ROI over 12 months (include payback month).
  * Security/Legal (Jasmin): SOC2 report, retention policies, KMS/HSM options, audit log granularity, data residency by region, sample redaction workflows for PII.
  * Infrastructure/Platform (Mike): latency SLOs, fallback & graceful degradation, dedicated capacity option for peak windows, network egress considerations.
- Ask list for Procurement/Legal (one page): sample contract term lengths, termination clauses, data handling appendix request, proof of controls (SOC2 + pen test summary), contact for SOC2 evidence.

Deliverables I’ll produce by Mon 2026-03-09 EOD PT:
- Champion one-pager (PDF)
- Procurement checklist (one-pager)
- Intro-ready email copy for Rishi to send to Dana

Marissa: please attach ROI_estimate_finserve.xlsx to the package when ready. I’ll also attach a redlined SLC appendix template (SLC_appendix.docx) and a short MoA draft (FinServe_MOA_v1.pdf) for their procurement to review.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
--
Attachments to follow: SLC_appendix.docx (draft), FinServe_MOA_v1.pdf (draft)

From: Dana Lewis <dana.lewis@finserve.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps — stakeholder map & champion enablement for FinServe POC

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the clear asks. A few notes from my side so you can tailor the playbook and materials to Procurement/Legal: 

Procurement/Timing:
- Procurement will need a one-page checklist and a sample SOW; I’ve copied Mike (procurement lead) who will run internal review.
- Target procurement review week of 2026-03-20; budget window closes 2026-03-25 as discussed.

Security/Legal info requested:
- Jasmin would like SOC2 Type II (last 12 months), pen test summary (latest), and a redlined SLC appendix. She prefers to review materials before an exec meeting.

Contacts (for clarity):
- Mike Turner, Procurement <m.turner@finserve.com>
- Jasmin Patel, Legal <jpatel@finserve.com>

I can act as the internal champion for the POC, but I’ll need the one-pager and a short deck (3 slides) that I can show in a 15-minute internal sync with Procurement + Legal next Tuesday (2026-03-16).

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call next Tue morning PT if it helps.

Dana
Head of AI Programs | FinServe

No attachments on my reply.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dana Lewis <dana.lewis@finserve.com>
Cc: Mike Turner <m.turner@finserve.com>, Jasmin Patel <jpatel@finserve.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps — stakeholder map & champion enablement for FinServe POC

Appreciate the clarity, Dana — and thanks for volunteering to champion the POC. Quick confirmation of next steps and what we’ll send you before Tue 2026-03-16 (your internal sync):

What you’ll receive by Mon 2026-03-15 EOD PT:
- Champion one-pager (PDF) tailored to Procurement + Legal (includes 3 short talk tracks).
- 3-slide deck for your 15-min sync: 1) TL;DR value + impact; 2) ROI snapshot (payback / 12-month view); 3) security & procurement checklist. (Attachment: ROI_estimate_finserve.xlsx referenced)
- SOC2 Type II summary and pen test executive summary (we will attach a sanitized summary for initial review).
- Redlined SLC appendix (SLC_appendix.docx) and a draft MoA (FinServe_MOA_v1.pdf) to speed procurement.

Champion enablement talking points (short bullets you can use in internal sync):
- ROI opener: "Based on your scale and our conservative batching assumptions, we estimate a 28–34% decline in unit inference cost. That translates to ~$21k–$28k savings per month at 1.2M requests (model mix dependent), with payback expected within 3–6 months after reserved capacity commit."
- Risk/controls: "We provide SOC2 Type II evidence, customer-configurable retention windows, and KMS integrations — Jasmin will have access to a redlined SLC appendix and pen test summary."
- Ops: "For peak windows we recommend a small Dedicated pool during business hours (12–18% of capacity) plus autoscale burst; this keeps P95 latency under 1.2s in our benchmarks for comparable workloads."

Ask for Procurement/Legal (to bring to your sync):
- Procurement: preferred term (12 v 24 months), desired SLA targets & remedies, PO vs SOW path, and billing cadence.
- Legal: any mandatory contract language re: retention, data processing addenda, or special compliance obligations.

Please confirm the Tue 2026-03-16 morning slot if you want us on the call; otherwise we’ll prepare all materials for you to present.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
--
Attachments included in follow-up package: ROI_estimate_finserve.xlsx, SLC_appendix.docx, FinServe_MOA_v1.pdf
